title: Canonical local-ring structure and ring maps on geometric strict henselizations
statement: For a scheme $S$ and a geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ [def-weil-geometric-point], use the canonical local-ring structure on $A^{\rm sh}_{S,\bar s}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Given a morphism of schemes $f:V\to S$ and a geometric point $\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$, define the ring map $f^{\rm sh,\#}:A^{\rm sh}_{S,f\bar v}\to A^{\rm sh}_{V,\bar v}$ as the pullback on global sections of the canonical induced strict-localization morphism, using the canonical spectrum/global-sections identifications. Here the induced morphism is the one specified by pulling back pointed etale neighbourhoods, compatible with the structural morphisms of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. For a displayed compatible point $\bar s$ and equality $h:f\bar v=\bar s$, define $f^{\rm sh,\#}_h:A^{\rm sh}_{S,\bar s}\to A^{\rm sh}_{V,\bar v}$ by equality transport of this same map. These are the canonical maps, with no smoothness, Noetherianity or flatness hypothesis.
